claims: The Artemis II mission is designed to last approximately 10 days.
The Artemis II mission has a crew of four astronauts.
The Artemis II mission crew will travel around the Moon and return to Earth.
The Artemis II mission flight lasts just over a week.
The Artemis II mission marks the first crewed deep-space mission in over 50 years.
The Artemis II mission is launched via SLS rocket on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission crew will spend about two days in high Earth orbit testing systems.
The Artemis II mission spacecraft will perform a "free-return" trajectory.
The Artemis II mission spacecraft will loop around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission spacecraft will use gravity to return to Earth.
The Artemis II mission crew will pass approximately 4,000 miles from the lunar surface.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to conclude with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is a test flight of the Orion spacecraft's life support systems.
